notes: Terrain Effects Chart (SPI 8.37): hex terrain, hexside features (cp is additive, the chart's '+'), fortification levels and minefields. Column shifts are signed: negative = L (columns to the left, favouring the defender), positive = R. 'gravel' here is the same terrain as 'sand-gravel' on the Construction Chart (construction.json)

Printed as in 1979: track costs 1 CP with footnote 8 and footnote 4 sits on Swamp. SPI's September 1979 errata (E-031) moves footnote 4 to Major City and says tracks do not cost 1 CP — they halve the hex terrain's cost (footnote 8 is correct, the '1' is not); the overlay data/errata/E-031.json applies both

The chart is on a page of the rulebook (jp2 69), not the shared chart sheet. Transcribed from the archive.org scan and cross-checked cell by cell against the community's OCR-converted scan of the 1979 rulebook (scan:discord:CampaignNorthAfrica - converted.pdf:p70): 0 of 27 rows differ. Clay Stone's errata-integrated Land rules PDF prints 'see Charts and Tables' with the two errata sentences in place of the chart

footnotes.1: a garrison unit in its assigned hex takes no stacking space; anti-aircraft units take none in a major city (any number), at an airfield (up to three) or at a landing strip (one)
footnotes.2: enterable and leavable, by track only, for light trucks, recce and motorcycle infantry — no other vehicle; nothing motorised fights into or out of a salt marsh (8.44)
footnotes.3: light trucks, motorcycle recce and motorcycle infantry may not enter, even by track
footnotes.4: Alexandria and Cairo hexes are level-three fortifications; every other one is level two
footnotes.5: Commonwealth units may be able to use rail movement (8.7)
footnotes.6: negates all hexside entry costs and breakdown values
footnotes.7: counts only what is actually on the road or track: the units and truck points using it in that hex at that moment
footnotes.8: halves all terrain entry costs and all hex and hexside breakdown values, except the CP and breakdown of a vehicle going down an escarpment
footnotes.9: motorised units and trucks may cross only on a track
footnotes.10: in a rainstorm may be crossed only where a road or railroad (treated as a road) crosses the hexside, at +2 CP
footnotes.11: may be crossed only where a road or railroad crosses the hexside; a motorised unit then pays no CP or breakdown for it
footnotes.12: armour targets get the defensive benefit only in a major city hex
footnotes.13: engineers cut the entry cost (26.2); assaulting forces standing in an enemy minefield give the non-phasing side L1 on anti-armour and close assault unless it already has them from a friendly minefield
